title: Response Patterns and Shoulder-tap Notebook — Nov 09 2027
content:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight, conversational notebook capturing the past week’s on-call response patterns, small experiment notes, and open questions that came up during shoulder-tap conversations. The goal is to preserve informal troubleshooting heuristics and surface observability gaps before they become deterministic incidents.

Summary (high level):
- Two medium-severity incidents this week (see INC-4821 and related thread). Both were tail-latency spikes caused by unexpected KV-cache churn during a sudden shift of long-context requests from a single customer.
- SLOs held overall, but we saw transient error-rate and p50/p95 regressions in EU region between 2027-11-06 03:00–03:27 UTC. No customer-facing SLA breach after fallbacks kicked in.
- Shoulder-tap pattern: junior on-call engineers often reached for manual restarts of model workers before checking the cache eviction and routing logs. That pattern produced avoidable noise.

Incident notes (INC-4821):
- Trigger: spike in 99th percentile inference latency for model-redwood-v1 on eu-west-1.
- Timeline (approx):
  - 03:02 UTC: latency alert fired (p99 > 1.1s threshold)
  - 03:04 UTC: on-call paged, started runbook
  - 03:07 UTC: initial remediation: autoscaler added workers (no immediate effect)
  - 03:12 UTC: Marcus observed concurrent high KV-cache eviction rate and cache-miss storms in the tracing view
  - 03:18 UTC: routed a fraction of traffic to a quantized variant (model-redwood-v1-q4) as fallback — latency normalized by 03:22 UTC
  - 03:27 UTC: alert closed, post-incident notes opened
- Root cause hypothesis: a customer workload with long prompt prefixes (avg sequence length +30%) caused excessive KV cache churn, invalidating locality assumptions in our prefix cache and pushing memory pressure leading to scan/evictions that amplified tail latency.
- Short-term mitigations applied: tweak cache size threshold for long-context sessions to avoid immediate eviction storms; enable aggressive fallback routing for customers that exceed 2x expected sequence length.
- Follow-ups (owners):
  - Increase KV cache telemetry granularity (owner: Lina, due: 2027-11-16)
  - Add a Canary rule for long-context sessions to route to low-latency variants sooner (owner: Rohit, due: 2027-11-14)
  - Run a controlled load test with synthetic long-prefix requests to validate eviction behavior (owner: Elena, due: 2027-11-18)

SLO snapshot and concerns:
- Current SLO: 99.5% requests under 1s p50/p95 baseline across hosted API (global).
- This week: cumulative SLO at 99.6% (good), but EU p99 saw 0.6 percentage point drift during the mid-week window.
- Observability gaps: no easy way to correlate per-customer prefix-length distribution with cache eviction rates in a single dashboard. This makes causal triage slow.
- Proposed quick win: add a lightweight tag (session_prefix_bucket) in traces for requests > 1k tokens and surface it in the latency dashboard (owner: Lina, due: 2027-11-16).

On-call handoffs and shoulder-tap patterns observed:
- Handoff friction: morning shift to overnight shift handoffs missed a single known-but-unresolved action item (change to fallback routing) that caused duplicate troubleshooting later. Need a mandatory open-action section in Handoff notes.
- Shoulder-tap observations:
  - Junior responders defaulted to worker restarts for perceived stuck workers; more time should be spent checking routing and cache-miss metrics.
  - Suggested mitigation: add a 2-minute checklist in the runbook for tail-latency alerts that enumerates: check cache-miss rate, check routing fallback status, confirm autoscale events, then consider restarts. (owner: Rohit, due: 2027-11-13)

Small experiments & heuristics tried this week:
- 'Soft-fence' for long-context sessions: temporarily mark sessions approaching 2x baseline length and begin gradual KV cache isolation to reduce eviction blast radius. Early anecdotal result: reduced p99 by ~12% in test buckets. (notes: experiment on canary group only; owner: Elena)
- Fallback aggressiveness tuning: lowered the fallback latency threshold by 15% during hours of high load. Observed fewer alert escalations, but slightly increased cost due to more traffic routed to quantized variants. Need cost-quality analysis. (owner: Marcus)

Open questions / unresolved puzzles:
- How to quantify the cost trade-off for routing more traffic to quantized variants automatically? Can we rely on downstream quality metrics (eval prompts) to signal rollback?
- Should we create a dedicated per-customer prefix-length quota to throttle pathological workloads at the edge, or is routing/fallback sufficient?
- Ops deck addition request: a quick matrix showing which model variants are safe for auto-fallback by route (owner: Product/Runtime team; request submitted in SRE-897)

Action items (short list):
- Add session_prefix_bucket to traces + dashboard (Lina) — due 2027-11-16
- Run controlled long-prefix load test (Elena) — due 2027-11-18
- Add 2-minute triage checklist to runbook and make it visible in handoff template (Rohit) — due 2027-11-13
- Create cost-quality dashboard for fallback routing (Marcus + Product) — due 2027-11-21

Handoff summary for next shift (2027-11-10 morning):
- Active items: KV cache telemetry enhancement (Lina), fallback rule drafting (Rohit), load test planning (Elena).
- Current risk: elevated p99 tail risk for customers with long-context workloads — mitigated by temporary fallback rules.
- Contact chain: on-call primary — Marcus; backup — Elena; escalation — Lina.

Notes to self / cultural items:
- Keep preserving small, informal troubleshooting heuristics — they’re often how new responders learn the system. This document is deliberately conversational so these patterns are discoverable.
- Encourage pairings on shoulder-taps: if a junior responder reaches for a restart, ask for a 5-minute pair-debug with a senior before full restart when feasible.

Meeting decisions and schedule:
- Quick sync scheduled: Friday 2027-11-12 16:00 UTC — topic: formalizing long-context handling in runtime and routing. Invite: SRE + Serving Runtime + Product. (owner: Rohit)
- Biweekly review: move latency-canary review to Monday mornings to catch long-weekend pattern shifts (owner: Lina)

Appendix (links and small logs):
- Short traces from the event were attached to INC-4821 and moved to the incident folder.
- Helpful query: "kv_cache_eviction_rate by session_prefix_bucket" — saved as a dashboard panel.

End of notebook.

(Informal notes; treat as living doc — add shoulder-tap anecdotes and heuristics as they happen.)
